items.title: Poor health of Yamuna reflects everything wrong with civic administration: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently observed that the deteriorating condition of the Yamuna river mirrors the failures of civic administration along its banks [ NOIDA v. State of UP & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan noted that pollution in the Yamuna continues to worsen despite massive public expenditure. "Everything that is wrong with civic administration in the towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the Court said. It invoked the doctrine of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) to hold States and Union Territories accountable if water quality degrades within their borders. "If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a State/Union Territory or a District therein, then that State/Union Territory or District within the State/Union Territory shall be held accountable and penalised," the Court warned.
